shock_mechanism: Port destruction: all container terminals damaged
channels: Container rerouting to Osaka/Yokohama and foreign ports
notes: Japan's largest container port effectively shut: Feb 1995 exports ~20% of prior year. National manufacturing dip was brief; traffic permanently diverted (Kobe never regained #6 world rank - structural loss, not cascade). Out of graph: JPN has no shipping/port node in the current 12x6 graph and the 1995 economy predates the 2019 calibration.

shock_mechanism: European airspace closure: >84% flights cancelled at peak; ~40% of EU air cargo affected
notes: 8-day airspace closure, 107k flights cancelled (~48% of zone traffic). Airlines lost ~$1.7-1.8bn; BMW/Nissan reported brief line stoppages from missing air-freighted parts. NEAR-MISS for manufacturing: sea freight (99% of EU goods volume) unaffected; production loss not measurable at national scale. Out of graph: no aviation nodes.

shock_mechanism: HGV-driver labor shortfall ~45-50k (~15% of pool); panic buying drained forecourts
notes: NEAR-MISS: 0% production capacity offline - refineries/terminals had ample stocks; the constraint was drivers + panic demand (forecourts dry within days, military tankers deployed Oct 4, normalized by end-Oct). No published production or US-inflation impact. Out of graph: GBR is not a graph country; labor-pool shocks are outside the model's mechanism set.

NEAR-MISS for industry: Rhine-based majors (BASF, Bayer, Thyssenkrupp) explicitly NOT hit; damage concentrated in residential/infrastructure. National industrial output showed no flood-attributable national-scale loss. Out of graph: no measurable source-side industry shock to encode - kept as the cleanest documented false-positive in the set.

shock_mechanism: Export licensing: China = 98% of primary gallium, ~60% germanium; exports fell to ~0 for ~2 months
sources: USGS Minerals Yearbook 2022/MCS 2024; CRMA 2024; US ITC trade data 2023
notes: NEAR-MISS: exports Jul->Aug 6876kg->0 (Ga), then licensing resumed (Oct 227kg). Feared chip disruption did not materialize: tiny volumes, downstream stockpiles, recycling and substitution absorbed it; prices spiked then eased. Out of graph: raw-material export channel (not production capacity) - below the granularity of the current industry nodes.
